managerCheckpoints: Observe whether every arriving customer is acknowledged promptly
Listen for a complete introduction and a transition question
Coach the salesperson who stays behind the desk or uses a passive let me know
coachingNotes: Use a brief welcome immediately, even when finishing another task
Start with the customer and purpose, not the transaction. Never open with What can I sell you or a price question
Escort, introduce and transfer useful context instead of handing the customer off without an introduction
Accept just looking, then ask one low-pressure discovery question instead of letting it end the conversation
Prompt does not mean aggressive. Acknowledge the customer quickly, then match their pace

Debrief role-play by asking what created trust, where the salesperson advanced too quickly and what exact phrase should be repeated or replaced. End with one behavior each participant will apply on the next customer

roleplayLabs.title: The Customer Who Wants Space
roleplayLabs.scenario: The customer enters slowly, avoids eye contact and says We're just looking. The salesperson must welcome them, reduce pressure and earn one discovery question. Roles: salesperson, customer and observer scoring pace, posture and transition.
evaluationCriteria: Salesperson does not argue with just looking
Conversation advances to a use or category question
No price promise or product dump

signoffCriteria: Approaches promptly without crowding the customer
Uses a consistent introduction that earns the customer's name and purpose
Transitions naturally into Interview and Discovery
Recognizes body-language and pace cues without surrendering leadership

managerCheckpoints: Review whether CRM notes contain useful discovery, not just looking for side-by-side
Ask the salesperson to state the customer's top three priorities before approving unit selection
Coach missing questions one at a time instead of demanding a longer interrogation
coachingNotes: Use follow-up questions connected to the customer's last answer instead of asking a checklist of questions without listening
Explain the purpose of financing questions and offer options without assuming the customer will be offended
Clarify who will use the unit and who must be comfortable with the decision
Repeat the priorities and earn agreement before selecting. Never show inventory before summarizing
Good discovery is a conversation with direction. Ask, listen, clarify and summarize
Do not ask for information that has no purpose. Explain why sensitive questions matter

roleplayLabs.title: Discovery Without Interrogation
roleplayLabs.scenario: The customer says they want something affordable for weekend use but provides limited detail. The salesperson must uncover use, users, must-haves, trade, timing and purchase structure. Roles: salesperson, customer with hidden priorities and observer tracking open and closed questions.
evaluationCriteria: At least five useful facts are uncovered
No unit is selected until discovery is complete

signoffCriteria: Conducts a conversational needs assessment
Captures useful notes without making the customer feel interrogated
Identifies use, users, priorities, trade, timing and purchase structure
Summarizes the discovery and earns permission to select a unit

managerCheckpoints: Require a concise customer brief before the salesperson leaves the desk
Use the introduction to learn the customer's name and confirm one priority
Track manager contacts and unsold customers who left without a manager conversation
coachingNotes: Require the salesperson to explain the unit match in the customer's words. Never select the unit before discovery
Make the manager introduction early and routine, not a rescue after the salesperson has lost control
The manager strengthens the salesperson, then returns ownership. The manager must not take over and sideline the salesperson
Begin with one deliberate choice and add a second only for a reason. Too many choices create confusion
No customer should leave without manager contact when dealership policy requires it

roleplayLabs.title: The First Choice
roleplayLabs.scenario: Using a completed discovery worksheet, the salesperson briefs the manager, introduces the manager and presents one first-choice unit. Roles: salesperson, manager, customer and observer.
evaluationCriteria: Manager receives a concise customer brief
Unit selection is tied to priorities
Plan B is mentioned without creating confusion

signoffCriteria: Selects a first-choice unit based on stated priorities
Uses a purposeful desk touch and manager introduction
Explains the manager's value without weakening the salesperson
Prepares a credible Plan B without overwhelming the customer

managerCheckpoints: Use daily walkarounds to assign one FFB to each salesperson
Ask why does that matter to this customer whenever a salesperson recites a specification
Correct inaccurate product claims immediately
coachingNotes: Limit the presentation to relevant priorities and value-building support instead of reciting the brochure
Require every major feature to end with which means so the benefit is stated
Verify the fact and explain the source rather than making claims the salesperson cannot support
Create customer interaction and check-in questions instead of talking continuously
Involve the customer. Opening, touching, sitting, loading, connecting and comparing create ownership
End by summarizing the three strongest reasons this unit fits

roleplayLabs.title: Turn Specifications into Value
roleplayLabs.scenario: The trainer assigns a product feature and a customer use. The salesperson must deliver three different FFB explanations for three different customer profiles. Roles: salesperson, customer profile reader and observer.
evaluationCriteria: Customer is invited to interact or respond

signoffCriteria: Explains the difference between a feature, function and benefit
Builds a presentation around discovery instead of reciting every specification
Uses an organized walkaround that fits the product category
Confirms value with customer participation and questions

managerCheckpoints: Approve routes and verify policy compliance
Observe whether demos actually occur or are replaced with parking-lot conversations
Review one buying signal with the salesperson before numbers are presented
coachingNotes: Use an approved route and product-specific safety policy. Never improvise an unsafe route
Allow quiet experience, then ask focused questions instead of talking through the entire customer drive
Demonstrate responsibly and within dealership and manufacturer guidance. No extreme capability demonstrations
Ask an ownership question and transition directly to the Trial Close instead of returning without confirming fit
Safety, licensing, waivers, protective equipment and dealership policy are never optional
A presentation tells. A demonstration proves

roleplayLabs.title: Purposeful Demo
roleplayLabs.scenario: The salesperson must conduct a pre-drive briefing, demonstrate one relevant function, transfer control and ask two ownership questions. Roles: salesperson, customer, safety observer and value observer.

signoffCriteria: Prepares and leads a safe, purposeful demonstration
Uses the route to reinforce selected benefits
Transfers control to the customer according to dealership policy
Creates emotional ownership and gathers buying signals

managerCheckpoints: Ask the salesperson to report the customer's trial-close response before presenting numbers
Coach the difference between a buying signal and an assumption
Do not permit numbers to become the first serious commitment conversation
coachingNotes: Earn the trial close with discovery and demonstration first. Never ask before building value
Ask direct, natural questions and listen to the answer instead of using manipulative tag questions repeatedly
Clarify the concern before advancing. Never ignore a negative answer
Use small commitments to prevent surprises later instead of waiting for the final close
A trial close is a temperature check. It does not replace the final ask
A hesitant answer is useful information. Clarify the concern instead of arguing

roleplayLabs.title: The Honest Temperature Check
roleplayLabs.scenario: The customer likes the unit but says I'm not sure yet. The salesperson must use a trial close, clarify the concern and choose the correct next step. Roles: salesperson, customer and observer.

signoffCriteria: Recognizes natural moments for a trial close
Uses low-pressure questions that measure ownership and fit
Responds productively to a negative or uncertain answer
Avoids treating a trial close as the final close

managerCheckpoints: Coordinate with service and parts so the step is expected and supported
Observe whether salespeople edify accurately or use vague praise
Track skipped tours and the reason they were skipped
coachingNotes: Use a brief prepared introduction or alternate approved method instead of skipping the step because the store is busy
Focus on two or three ownership benefits instead of turning the tour into a long department presentation
Use only verified capabilities. Never offer services the dealership does not provide
Share the customer's use and likely ownership need instead of introducing the customer without context
Edification must be genuine and specific. False praise feels scripted
The introduction should be brief, prepared and relevant to ownership

roleplayLabs.title: Why Buy Here?
roleplayLabs.scenario: The salesperson has two minutes to introduce service and parts and connect one capability to the customer's stated use. Roles: salesperson, service or parts teammate, customer and observer.
evaluationCriteria: One relevant ownership benefit is connected
Transition back to the process is smooth

signoffCriteria: Explains why service and parts belong before finance
Delivers a concise tour or introduction without creating delay
Edifies dealership teammates and ownership resources
Connects retention benefits to the customer's intended use

managerCheckpoints: Inspect appraisal completeness before assigning value
Coach neutral condition language and stop beat up the trade tactics
Explain the market evidence behind the appraisal when appropriate
coachingNotes: Set the expectation that the appraiser determines the supported value. Never promise a value before the appraisal
Explain equity or negative equity only after both facts are known. Payoff is not proof of value
Document condition neutrally and respectfully. Never criticize the customer's trade
Use the walkaround with the customer to gather information and reduce surprises
The salesperson gathers facts; the approved manager or appraisal process determines value
Condition should be documented objectively, not dramatized to create fear

roleplayLabs.title: Trade Without Tension
roleplayLabs.scenario: The customer owes more than they expect the trade to be worth and says I need payoff. The salesperson must separate payoff, value and structure without arguing. Roles: salesperson, customer and appraisal observer.
evaluationCriteria: Payoff and value are explained separately

signoffCriteria: Separates payoff from market value
Conducts a professional walkaround and condition review with the customer
Captures complete trade information in the approved system
Uses neutral language and avoids devaluing games

managerCheckpoints: Review the pencil with the salesperson before presentation
Require a specific objection and conditional commitment on every return
Coach payment-only presentations and unclear trade and equity explanations
coachingNotes: Present calmly and let the customer respond. Never apologize for the numbers before presenting them
Pause after asking for commitment. Give the customer time to process
Return with the exact concern and commitment. Never change figures without manager approval
Keep price, trade, cash investment and payment structure clear and separate instead of focusing only on payment
Numbers should not be the first time the customer experiences value or commitment
Present the approved proposal exactly as structured. Do not improvise discounts, rates or payments

roleplayLabs.title: Clear Proposal, Clear Ask
roleplayLabs.scenario: The customer likes the unit but reacts to the monthly option. The salesperson must identify whether the issue is payment, cash investment, term, trade or overall value. Roles: salesperson, customer and manager observer.
evaluationCriteria: Concern is isolated before returning to the manager

signoffCriteria: Prepares with the manager and understands every figure before presenting
Uses consistent terminology and presentation order
Explains price, trade, cash investment and payment options accurately
Asks for a clear commitment and returns to the manager with useful information

managerCheckpoints: Make manager turnovers normal and professional, not dramatic
Ask the salesperson what the customer said verbatim before entering
Coach whether the objection was actually isolated and whether a clear reclose occurred
coachingNotes: Clarify and isolate first. Never answer before understanding
Respond to the actual concern in the customer's language instead of using a memorized comeback
Use only real availability or expiration information. Never create false scarcity
Respectfully clarify whether a no is final or based on a solvable concern instead of giving up after the first no
Use the J|13 Objection Loop: Listen, Clarify, Respond, Confirm, Reclose
Feel-Felt-Found can be useful when it is truthful and brief. Do not invent customer stories or use the technique to dismiss a legitimate concern
Match the closing technique to the moment: assumptive, summary, alternative choice, sharp-angle, if-I-could-would-you and legitimate urgency. Never manufacture urgency

roleplayLabs.title: Clarify Before You Answer
roleplayLabs.scenario: The customer says I need to think about it. The salesperson must discover whether the issue is product fit, timing, another decision participant, trade or money. Roles: salesperson, customer with assigned hidden concern and observer.
evaluationCriteria: At least two clarifying questions are used

signoffCriteria: Distinguishes a question, concern, objection and stall
Uses the J|13 Objection Loop
Applies closing techniques at the appropriate moment
Uses manager assistance without abandoning ownership of the customer
Documents the outcome and next step in the CRM

managerCheckpoints: Inspect whether every qualified customer receives the approved finance process
Coach salespeople who quote rates or discourage products
Use finance feedback to identify missing customer context in handoffs
coachingNotes: Explain the business manager's advisory and ownership role. Never call finance the paperwork person
Refer exact approval questions to finance. Never promise a rate or payment
Give every qualified customer a complete presentation. Never prejudge product interest or say you won't want that
Prepare delivery and complete the exit experience instead of dropping the customer at finance and taking another customer
Cash customers may still benefit from financing flexibility, protection products or liquidity; the conversation must remain factual and optional
Brief the business manager on use, ownership priorities, decision participants, trade, timing and any questions already asked

roleplayLabs.title: The Warm Handoff
roleplayLabs.scenario: The customer is paying cash and says they do not need finance. The salesperson must explain the complete review without pressure or promising value. Roles: salesperson, customer, business manager and observer.
evaluationCriteria: No product or approval is promised
Salesperson states what happens during finance

signoffCriteria: Explains the purpose of the business office accurately
Completes a warm handoff with useful customer context
Avoids pre-selling or disqualifying finance products
Supports cash-conversion conversations ethically and consistently

managerCheckpoints: Audit delivery checklists and promised-work completion
Review prior-day deliveries and unsold follow-up every morning
Listen for purposeful follow-up, not vague just checking in calls
coachingNotes: Complete the current customer experience or arrange an approved team handoff instead of rushing delivery because another customer arrived
Call with a specific purpose, update, question or piece of value instead of a generic checking in follow-up
Use the CRM as the system of record. Never count unlogged contact attempts
Honor a clear no-contact request and follow policy
Delivery is not the end of the sale. It is the beginning of ownership and the first proof that promises will be kept
Continue follow-up until the customer buys, clearly declines, chooses another option, requests no contact or moves into the dealership's long-term nurture plan

roleplayLabs.title: Delivery Teach-Back
roleplayLabs.scenario: The salesperson must deliver a unit, explain one safety-critical feature and use teach-back before setting the next-day follow-up. Roles: salesperson, customer and observer.
evaluationCriteria: Follow-up time and channel are set

signoffCriteria: Delivers the unit with a consistent checklist
Confirms paperwork, product operation and ownership resources
Sets the first follow-up expectation before the customer leaves
Uses a purposeful sold and unsold follow-up cadence recorded in the CRM

managerCheckpoints: Set visible activity standards and inspect CRM quality, not only totals
Confirm appointments personally and keep the appointment board current
Review prior-day unsold customers and missed appointments every morning
Recognize two-way contacts, shows and process quality as leading indicators
coachingNotes: Schedule protected daily outreach time instead of only prospecting when traffic is slow
Reference the customer, unit, timing or useful update instead of leaving generic voicemails with no reason to respond
Record the work in the CRM. Never count unlogged activity
Earn the referral through a strong experience, then ask directly. Never ask before creating value
Two-way contacts matter more than raw dials, but consistent activity creates those conversations
For commercial prospects, conduct a needs analysis, record equipment cycles and schedule a consistent follow-up plan tied to the business cycle rather than generic monthly calls

roleplayLabs.title: Appointment With a Reason
roleplayLabs.scenario: The salesperson receives an aged lead with no recent response. Create a call, voicemail, text and short video message that share one useful reason to reconnect. Roles: salesperson, prospect and observer.

signoffCriteria: Builds a daily prospecting rhythm with activity goals for calls, two-way contacts, appointments, confirmations and shows
Uses the CRM to manage outbound activity and long-term opportunities
Asks for referrals naturally throughout the ownership cycle
Applies the process to commercial and community prospects

weeklyCoachingRhythm: One recorded or live role-play per salesperson
One product FFB presentation per salesperson
Deal review: where process or value was lost
Recognition of process behaviors, not only deliveries
coreScorecard: Opportunities: fresh ups, leads, service opportunities, referrals and self-generated prospects
Contacts: calls, texts, emails, videos and meaningful two-way contacts
Appointments: set, manager-confirmed, shown and sold

Results: units, front gross, finance gross, products, total gross and customer experience
Follow-Through: CRM notes, lost reasons, scheduled tasks, sold follow-up and referral requests
managerDailyAudit: CRM notes and lost reasons complete
Most important coaching action today identified
oneOnOneGuide: Review the pipeline and aged opportunities
Review prior-day unsold customers before the opportunity goes cold
Review activity against goals: calls, two-way contacts, appointments, shows, deliveries and referrals
Identify specific obstacles and priorities for the day
Use coaching language: describe the observed behavior, explain the impact, demonstrate the correction, require a repetition and set a time to inspect it again
Avoid vague feedback such as be more aggressive or try harder
Recognize process behaviors, not only deliveries

requirements: Certification requires knowledge, demonstrated skill and manager commitment to reinforcement
Pass a seven-question knowledge assessment recorded as a knowledge score
Complete a practical assessment demonstrating all eleven process behaviors from Meet and Greet through the prospecting appointment call
Sign the J|13 Commitment stating the steps will not be treated as optional based on convenience, traffic level or personal habit, countersigned by the manager
Manager commits to inspect trained behaviors after the trainer leaves so training becomes visible on the floor and in the CRM
certification.knowledgeCheckStandard: Seven-question knowledge assessment: state the 13 steps in order; explain Feature, Function and Benefit; describe the purpose of the early Manager Introduction; explain the difference between trade value and payoff; state the five-step J|13 Objection Loop; describe the finance handoff standard; explain when follow-up should stop or change cadence. Each step module also includes its own written knowledge check.
certification.practicalEvaluation: Live demonstration of eleven behaviors: Meet and Greet and transition, Interview and Discovery summary, Manager Introduction, FFB presentation, Demo and Trial Close, Service and Parts Introduction, trade conversation, Present Numbers and close, finance handoff, delivery and follow-up and a prospecting appointment call. Role-play is scored on the Role-Play Observation Scorecard from 1 (not demonstrated) to 5 (consistent and natural) with a target of 4 or higher on all twelve criteria, scoring the behavior, not the personality.
certification.reassessment: The certification evaluation records a knowledge score, practical score, overall result and a reassessment date. Participants who do not meet the standard receive one behavior to repeat, one behavior to correct and a repetition deadline with manager inspection, then are reassessed on the scheduled date. The trainer rule applies: hearing a script once is exposure; performing it correctly, under pressure, with a real customer is mastery.

facilitation.deliveryModel: The Trainer Edition is a facilitation system, not a manual to be read aloud cover to cover. Every module is taught through explanation, demonstration, practice, observation and follow-through, with examples customized to the dealership's brands, inventory, CRM, forms, policies and customer base. The exact J|13 sequence is taught before personal variations in wording are allowed. Role-play builds skill, not embarrassment: start simple, add resistance and coach one behavior at a time. Managers must participate because a process without manager reinforcement becomes a short-term event. Commitments, assignments and observed behaviors are documented, and participant handouts are derived from this master edition so trainer and salesperson work from the same definitions. Onsite delivery follows a four-day plan: Day 1 Foundation and Control (J|13 overview, dealership teamwork, professional standards, Steps 1-3, live greeting and discovery practice, manager-introduction standard); Day 2 Build Value (Steps 4-7, inventory walkaround, FFB presentations, demo process, trial closes, service and parts introductions); Day 3 Structure the Decision (Steps 8-10, trade assessment, proposal presentation, objection loop, closing techniques, manager turnover practice); Day 4 Complete and Rebuild the Pipeline (Steps 11-13, finance handoff, delivery, follow-up, prospecting, commercial process, certification role-play, manager action plan). Each step module is estimated at 60-90 minutes with manual, participant worksheet, role-play scorecard and dealership-specific examples.
sessionStructure: Explain why the step matters to the customer, salesperson and dealership
Demonstrate the process and approved word tracks
Let participants practice in short repetitions
Observe the step with a real customer or live inventory
Debrief with specific feedback and assign a measurable behavior
Have the manager inspect the behavior after the trainer leaves

Use the Trainer Session Plan to define the objective, observable behavior, dealership-specific policy, demonstration plan, role-play resistance level and manager inspection commitment before each module

Close each training day with the Daily Recap: what was taught and practiced, what was observed on the floor, what improved immediately, what remains inconsistent or blocked, manager commitments before the next day or visit and the metrics or evidence that will confirm progress

Before onsite delivery complete the Trainer Preparation Checklist: meet with the dealer principal or GM to define outcomes and non-negotiables, review current process, forms, CRM, finance flow and manager roles, request prior-period metrics, confirm attendees, schedule, training space and live-floor observation access, select inventory for walkaround and demonstration practice, customize scripts only where dealership policy requires it and prepare daily recap and manager commitments
